lines.text: Don’t make me put it plainer. I’d go soppy, and then the wallpaper starts, and there’s no stopping the pair of us before supper.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Mrs. Bramble hums something old and out of tune, polishing a doorknob that was already bright.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: She catches you looking, winks, and goes on humming. The doorknob has never been brighter.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Before you go rattling doorknobs, pet — sit a moment. There’s a thing I’ve dusted around for years and never once said out loud.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Six candles at his desk, always six. Near the end he let one gutter out each night — and I never dared relight them. Some housekeeping isn’t yours to do.

lines.speaker: bramble
lines.text: Put it in your journal, pet. It’s evidence, even if saying it still feels like tidying his grave.

summary: Mrs. Bramble’s testimony: six candles, let out one by one.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Oh — footsteps. Real ones, with weight in them. How novel. Welcome to the Library; do come in, the dust is friendly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery. Librarian. The ‘late’ is silent, but I’ll spare us both the arithmetic — I’ve kept these shelves rather longer than a living person would.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ll want the tour: fiction sulks by the window, reference never sleeps, and the poetry cases are load-bearing. Do not test that last one.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And I shall want your opinions. On everything. I’ve had thirty years of my own and they’ve gone soft from no argument.

summary: Met Ellery, the librarian. The ‘late’ is silent.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Manners! Oh, I have missed manners. The manor mostly sends me weather, and the occasional moth.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Weather, moths, and once — memorably — a bat with opinions about Restoration drama. You will be a marked improvement.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Come by whenever the shelves confuse you. Confusion is the catalogue working; I merely translate.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Librarian first, ghost second. Death was only ever a change of department, and frankly the hours suit me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Don’t make the face, dear. I’m not cold spots and corridor-wailing. I am mostly filing, with occasional gloating.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The wailing section is upstairs anyway, and we do not lend from it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Mind the shelves — they rearrange overnight, same as the rooms. I reshelve by candlelight, and by morning the books pretend it was always so.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: If you find loose pages in odd rooms — his handwriting, ink gone brown — bring them where I can see them. I knew his hand better than my own.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Don’t take the rearranging personally. The house isn’t hiding things — it’s showing them to you in the wrong order. A librarian’s distinction, I grant, but I died for less.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: If a shelf refuses you outright, bow slightly and try again after tea. I wish I were joking. I have never once been joking about shelves.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And the pages — brown ink, a hand that slants left when it lies. You’ll know them when they hum at you.

summary: Ellery watches for the lexicographer’s loose pages.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’re carrying one of his pages — I can hear it. Paper with his ink on it hums a little flat. Keep it safe in the journal; it’s been alone a long while.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He wrote on anything, at the end. Flyleaves. Receipts. The backs of my overdue notices — which I have chosen to read as affection.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Where did this one turn up? No — don’t tell me. Let me guess from the water stains. It’s the last game he left me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring it to the lamp when you’ve a minute. Paper settles wonderfully once it’s been read properly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Another fragment? He scattered them like a man hiding pieces of his own heart from himself. Which, between us, is exactly what it was.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Look how the hand wavers there — he wrote that one late, and by a poor candle. You can date a sentence by its shivering.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Keep gathering. A heart in pieces is still a complete work; it only wants collating.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That line we read together keeps opening further, doesn’t it. Good annotation is like that — a little door drawn in a margin.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He’d have liked that you puzzle at his meaning instead of taking him at his word. He never once took himself at his word.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That is the whole tragedy, filed in a sentence. No charge.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A whole case sorted without one slip — the Library is preening. Shelves have feelings, you know. Mostly smug ones.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I have entered it in the ledger as ‘a good day, witnessed.’ The ledger has embarrassingly few of those entries. Guard your average.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Dewey supervised, of course. He’ll be claiming the credit by supper, and I shall let him. Seniority.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You put words back where they belong today. That’s the entire job, you know. It took me forty years and a death to learn it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I watched you work, by the by. Rude of me — but ghosts have no doorbells, so we make do with lurking.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You sort like he did. Impatient with the almost-right. Keep that; it is the entire difference between shelving a thing and hiding it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Rest your eyes tonight. The catalogue rewards the well-slept, and so, on my better days, do I.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You left a case half-sorted. Quite right — a puzzle keeps better than a person does. It will still be wrong tomorrow. That’s a promise, not a threat.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The books don’t mind, before you ask. Half of them waited thirty years for you; a night more is a rounding error.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Leave your place marked and your conscience unmarked. That’s the whole of my policy on unfinished business — present company included.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The whole house rang like a struck shelf when you spoke at that door. Not the word — but the ringing lasted longer this time. I count such things.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It rang truer, I mean. Wrong notes come in families, and I believe you have found the right family.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Go back through his margins tonight. He argued with himself in pencil, and the pencil usually won.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And eat something first. Revelation on an empty stomach reads as dizziness, and Bramble will blame me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ve offered the door that word before, dear. It kept the receipt. Doors and librarians never forget a request.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: No shame in it. I once reshelved the same atlas four days running and blamed the atlas.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: But do consult your journal, dear — that is precisely what the poor thing is for.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Word travels — every petal in one bloom, down in the Conservatory. Even the botany section is jealous, and it does not impress easily.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Fern will pretend she didn’t smile about it. She smiled. The ivy told the moth, and Chapman tells me everything.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A whole alphabet in one bloom. He’d have written it down twice — once to keep, once to lose somewhere you’d find it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ten rooms set right since you arrived. You turn this house like pages. I’ve opened a card for you in the catalogue — filed under ‘recurring joy.’

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The card has a proper number and a crest and everything. You may not borrow yourself; library policy is firm on that point.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ten rooms. He managed nine in his best week, and I recorded it, and now you know why my ledger locks.

summary: Ellery filed you in the catalogue under ‘recurring joy.’

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Posy’s seals again? She strings and stamps like the post is a sacrament. She’s right, of course. Never tell her I said so.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: She has kept that post longer than I have been dead — which, between us, constitutes a career.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Answer your mail, incidentally. The house files silence under ‘no’, and it sulks accordingly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Every book in this room sat up an inch when that door opened. I felt the spines straighten. Thirty years of slouching, undone in one word.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He can rest now. And I — well. I believe I shall finally read something for pleasure.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I keep starting novels and shelving them mid-sentence, out of vigilance. Habit. It will pass, I’m told, by people with less experience of ‘eventually’ than I have.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The carrel gets the morning light again. I hadn’t noticed it had stopped. Houses hold their breath so quietly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Come by the lamp anyway, won’t you? A library with its mystery finished still wants readers. Perhaps more than ever.

summary: The books sat up an inch. Ellery is reading for pleasure now.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ll want to know how I died. Everyone does, eventually. A storm, that chair, a very good book. I finished the chapter, closed my eyes, and simply — stayed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You needn’t look stricken. As deaths go, it was practically a recommendation for the book.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The chair is still here, if you’d like to try the sitting half of the experience. I recommend stopping there.

summary: Ellery finished the chapter, closed her eyes, and stayed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: So am I, most days. The manor is drafty, but the company has improved enormously of late.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He found me the next morning, you know. Put the book back himself — right shelf, right place, spine flush.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That was the eulogy, as far as I was concerned. Everything after was just weather.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A dictionary. Volume three, F through H. I have never once regretted it, which tells you everything about me worth shelving.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: F through H. ‘Grief’ is in there, you know. So is ‘home’. I have had time to notice the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: One shelf apart, those two. I used to think that was filing. Now I suspect it was a promise.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He worked at that desk till the candle drowned, most nights. Then one spring he stopped writing words down and started crossing one out. Everywhere. Every copy. Every margin.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I thought it was proofreading, at first. He was thorough that way. Then I saw which word he was drowning, and understood it was surgery.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A man can unwrite a word from every book in a house. He cannot unwrite it from the house. You have noticed that by now, I think.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I still hear the nib some nights. A little rasp, like a moth against glass, going from room to room being merciful.

summary: One spring, the lexicographer stopped writing and started crossing out.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I watched him ink out that word, and I said nothing. Librarians archive; we don’t intervene. It is the one entry in my whole catalogue I would amend.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I told myself it was respect. Grief deserves privacy, I said, and stamped it, and shelved it, and called the shelving kindness.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It was fear, of course. The catalogue is honest even when I am not.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: So intervene, dear — wherever you find a thing being quietly erased. Consider that an amendment to my rules. Consider it his.

summary: Ellery watched the erasure and said nothing. She regrets the silence.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: That fragment you carry — bring it to the lamp. Reading him alone is like shelving in the dark; together we might make out what he actually meant.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There. See how the sentence unclenched? He wrote in knots when he was ashamed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It says more than he meant and less than he felt. Most true things do.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring me the others as you find them. Two readers make a margin; one only makes an echo.

summary: Ellery read one of the fragments with you, by lamplight.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring today’s page to the lamp, then. His hand slants left when he’s lying to himself — you learn to read around that.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There — another knot out. He would be mortified, then grateful. In that order. Always in that order.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bring the next one sooner, won’t you. He reads easier while the last page is still warm in the hand.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Posy mentioned me? Meddling by mail — how efficient. Then I’ll confess it: one bookplate in this Library has lost its book, and I cannot rest an inch until it’s found.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Sort a whole case perfectly — not one slip — and I believe the shelves will surrender it. They respect precision. It’s their one romance.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Yes, I could search myself. I have tried. The shelves treat me as staff, and staff never get the good surprises.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It will be a small book. Green, I think, though memory paints. Mind the third case from the window; it bites.

summary: Ellery’s favor: sort a Library case perfectly to find the lost book.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There — do you hear it? A book just came home, three shelves over. Not a sound a living ear would catch. Lucky, then, that you brought me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The plate reads: ‘Ex libris — to E., who stayed.’ He made it for me. All these years, I never found the nerve to go looking.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: ‘Who stayed.’ He knew, then. All those years I thought my staying was a secret, and he had already sent it to the printer’s.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I shall keep it face-out on the desk, against every rule of conservation I hold dear. Some things are for reading, not keeping.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Thank you. I mean the word in its oldest binding — the one with weight in it.

summary: Found Ellery’s lost bookplate: ‘To E., who stayed.’

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: His carrel. I’ve kept it locked since — well. Since. You’ve earned the chair, and the chair has earned better company than a ghost’s.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Read what he underlined, some quiet evening. A man’s pencil is far honester than his pen.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And if his pencil says things about me — the atlas incident in particular — I was provoked, and the atlas knows it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Sit with the door open, won’t you? I like the lamplight in the aisle. It reads as company.

summary: Ellery unlocked the lexicographer’s private carrel for you.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ribbon. Gilt. A tassel, even. I have marked my place with regret for thirty years, dear, and you hand me this as though it were nothing.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Take my card in trade. The Library honors it anywhere in the manor. Which is to say: I vouch for you. Loudly, for a ghost.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Use it on something difficult, won’t you? Ribbon this good is wasted on a book you’d finish anyway.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: And yes, the card works after hours. Especially after hours. Libraries are mostly night, if we’re honest.

summary: Gave Ellery a bookmark; received her library card in trade.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I do love marginalia. A book tells you what an author thought; the margins tell you what a reader felt. Always read the pencil.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: His margins were full of arguments — with authors, with himself. Once, gloriously, with a recipe. The recipe was wrong, mind.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: When I go — further, I mean — I should like to be summarized in pencil, in a margin, by someone who read closely. That’s the whole ambition.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There’s a moth in the poetry section I’ve named Chapman. We have an arrangement: he eats only the reviews.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He has eaten three reviews of the master’s dictionary this month. I have never fed him better, and we are both a little ashamed.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Chapman stays out of the fragments, before you worry. Even a moth knows which paper is somebody’s heart.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Rain through a wall is a strange thing to miss. I can hear it, you understand. I simply can’t be rained on. Do stand in some for me.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There’s a window seat in the Gallery that takes the storm straight on the glass. Sit there once for me and don’t hurry off.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I’ll take the report after. Sound of it, smell of it, whether it got in your collar. Spare no detail; I have shelf-room.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The manor shelves itself by a system I’ve almost cracked. Twice I’ve found the atlases hiding in Biography — which is either an error or a thesis.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: My working theory is that the house shelves by feeling. Atlases in Biography, because maps are lives. It is an error. It is also correct.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: When I crack the system fully I expect to find one empty shelf at the center, labeled in his hand. I try not to guess the label.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Bramble still pours a second cup at four o’clock and lets it go cold. It’s mine. We don’t discuss it, and you mustn’t either.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Steam curls differently over a cup that is meant for someone. That is not science. It is merely true.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Drink yours while it’s hot, incidentally. Cold tea is for the dead, and we’re territorial about it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The cat outranks me, technically. Dewey — as in the decimal system. He enforces it by sitting on exceptions.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He occupied the returns bin for nine days once, until I apologized. I still don’t know what for. Neither does he. It’s the principle of the thing.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Between us, he cannot actually read. Do not tell him. He sits on the dictionaries with such conviction.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Three of his pages now, is it? Read them together, in order, until one of them answers another. That is the signal, dear — not certainty. Correspondence. Then go up and say it like you mean it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A wrong word does no harm up there, dear. The door refuses gently — I have heard it do it. It learned refusal from him, and he only ever refused himself.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: When you do go up, go fed and unhurried. Words arrive better to a body that isn’t braced.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Closing, dear. Not the library — that never closes. Me. I have one good conversation in a day and you have just had it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Take a book with you, if you like. The trust is the point — the reading is merely encouraged.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I’ll put myself back on the shelf now. Even a ghost keeps hours — eccentric ones, but firm.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Come tomorrow and I’ll have finished the thought I started. Ghosts think slowly. The thoughts are worth the wait.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: She is already drifting back toward the shelves, straightening spines as she goes.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery drifts along a high shelf, tapping spines flush without quite touching them.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: If you must haunt the doorway, dear, do it one step in. You’re letting the quiet out.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: A book lies open on the desk. The pages turn themselves, patiently, one sigh at a time.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery glances up, marks her place with a finger that touches nothing, and nods you on your way.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I have catalogued this room down to its dust, dear, and there was never a card for the sound of somebody arriving on purpose. I have had to write one out fresh.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Dreadful card. Wobbling letters, wrong hand entirely. I wrote it in a hurry, and I have not hurried since 1931.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Another bookmark? You are single-handedly reforming my relationship with stopping. I used to dog-ear, you know. In life. The confessions this house drags out of one.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It goes with the others — I keep them in Volume Three, F through H, so the best words get the company.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Now off you go before I waive your fines out of sentiment. ...They were waived the day we met. Don’t tell the ledger.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The catalogue asked me to re-file you this morning. Closer to the front. I don’t argue with the catalogue when it’s right.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: This is me being demonstrative, by the way. Librarians emote in classification.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Now — what shall we read you next? Don’t answer. I’ve been planning it for days.

summary: Re-filed closer to the front of Ellery’s catalogue.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I’ve been mending a broken spine all week. Linen, paste, patience. Mostly patience.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You can’t make a damaged book new. You can make it whole. The two get confused by people who have never been either.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It’ll outlive the both of us. Well. You. It’ll outlive you. I intend to check on it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Linen tape, wheat paste, and a weight of your own choosing. Everything I know about mending is in that sentence, dear — books or otherwise.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: We keep one first edition so rare I’ve never told the house where it is. The house pretends not to know. We are both lying and it’s very companionable.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: No, I shan’t say which book. A librarian with no secrets is just furniture that alphabetizes.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Earn a few more years of my acquaintance and we’ll see.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Dust is just the house thinking. It settles thickest where nobody’s finished grieving — that isn’t poetry, it’s observation. The Study, for instance.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I don’t clear it anymore. Seemed rude. Like interrupting.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The feather duster is kept for ceremonial duties only. We have both retired into pageantry.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The Study’s is deepest. I measured it once with a ribbon and then felt ashamed of myself, which is unusual, and which I did not enjoy.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The green lamp was his. It lights when someone’s reading honestly — skimmers get flicker. I don’t make the rules; I only enjoy them.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It’s been steady all week, since you started coming by. I’ve told the lamp it’s being obvious.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Sit under it whenever you like. It misses honest work.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It flickered for him, at the end. I have never told a soul that, and now I have told you, so do mind the lamp.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: There are eleven kinds of quiet in this library. I’ve catalogued them. Reading-quiet, waiting-quiet, snow-quiet.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: The twelfth arrived the year he died and refuses classification. It sits in the Study, mostly.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ve been thinning it, for what it’s worth. Whatever you’re doing — it files under ‘remedy’.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Name them yourself as you go. A quiet you can name stops being a quiet you are stuck inside.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: I read endings first. Yes, I know. Thirty years dead and still getting letters about it.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: It isn’t impatience. A librarian ought to know where a thing is headed before recommending the road.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Yours, I haven’t peeked at. Some books you’d rather read at the author’s pace.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Though if you insist on knowing how yours goes: badly, then well, then quietly, on a Thursday. All the good ones go about like that.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Ellery runs a cloth along a shelf without disturbing a single mote. The gesture is the point.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: You’ve been filling that journal. Good. Then you’re ready for the thing he said to me that I have shelved and reshelved for years without ever finding it a place.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: He told me once that in all the dictionary there is exactly one word that names the hole it would leave behind. I laughed. Librarians laugh at paradoxes; it’s a professional hazard.

lines.speaker: ellery
lines.text: Then he went and made it true. Write it down exactly as I said it. The wording matters — with him it always did.

summary: Ellery’s testimony: one word names the hole it would leave.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Customer! No — guest! No — resident? Oh, I’ll open you a file either way. Posy, postmistress. The house writes letters overnight and I sort where they land.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Don’t mind the avalanche — that’s the Unclaimed pile. Fifty years of letters for rooms that wandered off mid-delivery. They’ll turn up. Rooms always do, and mail outlives embarrassment.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Now. First stamp’s free, first cup of tea is mandatory, and the kettle’s just gone. Sit.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Name for the file? No — don’t tell me. The house already wrote it on your pigeonhole. It has never once misspelled anybody.

summary: Met Posy, the postmistress. You have a file now.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Excellent attitude. Under ‘permanent address’ I shall put ‘wherever the house sets them down’ — same as everybody in this file. You’ll have mail by morning; the house is a terrible gossip in writing.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: There — filed. You’ve a pigeonhole now, third row, next to the Conservatory’s. It gets pollen on its neighbors, but good ones are worth the dusting.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Come by after breakfast, always. News lands overnight. So do opinions.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The house, mostly. Old friends of the master. The odd bill, which I file under ‘fiction.’ You’ll see — check with me after breakfast.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Oh, and the occasional letter from a room to another room. The Gallery and the Study correspond. It’s frosty this decade.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The Study writes to no one, mind. Never has. We all pretend not to notice, the way you do with a quiet uncle.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You’ll come to like it, or you’ll come to like complaining about it. Both count as settling in, love.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: House rules of the Post Room: string is sacred, brown paper is reusable, and nothing marked ‘urgent’ ever is. The truly urgent arrives unstamped.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Rule the fourth: if Dewey is asleep on a parcel, the parcel waits. I fought that battle in ’61 and the scars are administrative.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Rule the fifth — and this one’s yours specially: anything in his brown ink comes straight to a friendly face. Mine’s on duty, Ellery’s is on lamplight.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: That’s the lot. Everything else in this room runs on string and affection, same as me.

summary: Learned the Post Room rules. String is sacred.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Opened your post, did you? Good. An unread letter is just a secret with a stamp on it, and secrets curdle.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I could tell it was a good one from the way the envelope sat. Good news perches. Bad news lies flat.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Well — go on about your day. The post loves a busy addressee.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And write back sometime. The house checks the outgoing tray every morning. It has never once found anything in it, and it looks anyway.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: That seal came out of my good wax, I’ll have you know. Crimson. I save it for letters that matter — and I am rarely wrong about which do.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The house asked for the good wax, mind — I just held the spoon. It has opinions about you. Nice ones, lately.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Wax readings are free with every delivery. Interpretations of the actual letter cost tea.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You read this morning’s letter? I don’t peek, officially. Unofficially: the house presses harder with its pen when it likes you.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Handwriting analysis, free of charge: the loops say fondness, the crossings-out say it drafted that letter four times. Houses get nervous too, you know.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Keep them, by the way. Letters like being kept. It’s the one thing paper and people agree on.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And I’m told nothing, officially. Unofficially, my ears are the best-sorted things in this room.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: A wrong word at that door posts itself straight back — return to sender, no postage owed. The right one gets delivered. Keep writing, love.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I heard the knocker jump from down here. Don’t you go quiet over it — a returned letter isn’t a lost one. Different bins entirely.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Redraft. The best correspondents are just the stubbornest ones with better spelling.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And if the door’s feeling smug, remind it who oils its hinges. We keep accounts, the door and I.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: A scrap of his hand turned up? Naturally. This house never lost a page in its life — it only ever forwards them. Everything arrives eventually.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Give it here a moment — just to hold. ...His hand, all right. Heavier down-strokes than his letters had. He pressed harder when it mattered.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: File it with the journal, and mind the corners. Some post takes thirty years to find its addressee, and it’s rude to bend it on arrival.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Paper’s only half a thing till somebody reads it. You’re the other half now.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Someone’s beaming down the corridor about a certain little gift. I’d never name names. I have a face that names them for me.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: It’s good practice, gifting. Keeps the house’s arteries clear. Affection clots if you hoard it — that’s medical fact, postal division.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ll note the date in the ledger. Under ‘nice things, unprompted.’ We’re building quite the file on you.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Keep it up and this house will be unbearable with contentment. I look forward to complaining.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: A flawless room. Nothing returned, nothing queried, not one item mislaid. Fifty years at this counter, love, and I know clean work when it crosses it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The room’s letter arrived before you did — glowing, if slightly smug about its own floorboards.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: For the record: the Post Office defines ‘first-class’ by handling. You handle things first-class. That’s the entire review.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Keep it up and I’ll need a bigger commendation drawer. Don’t keep it up on my account. Keep it up on yours.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You look posted through a hedge, if I’m honest. Long day yesterday? The manor over-delivers. It gets it from me.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Sit a minute before you launch off. The morning sort can watch us both do nothing; it’s very educational for the mail.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And drink water. Postmistress’s orders. Yes, we can order that. There’s a form.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The mail ran itself ragged once too. 1953. We don’t speak of the Great Overdelivery, except to say: sit down, love.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: There’s a chair behind my counter with fifty years of sitting worn into it. Borrow it. It knows the job better than either of us.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You’re becoming rather dear to this household, you know. It shows in the mail volume. Affection is measurable; I keep charts.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Today’s haul: two notes about you, one poem — unsigned, terrible meter, lovely sentiment — and a pressed flower I suspect is Fern being demonstrative.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Charts don’t lie. Well — mine don’t. I refuse to draw a dishonest axis.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Keep on as you are. Everything’s pointing up and to the dear.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The morning it happened, every dead letter in my bins went light. Years of undeliverables — suddenly addressed. All of them his. All of them home.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I cried on the franking machine, and I would do it again. Now sit down and let me stamp your hand like a parcel. Tradition. New one. Starting now.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The stamp washes off in a day or two. The standing in this house does not. You’re franked, love — official, first-class, no further postage owed.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: One of those dead letters was his, you know. To the house itself. It just says thank you. I read it aloud in the empty sorting room, and the floor creaked back.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: There. Now you know everything the Post Office knows. Took me fifty years, and it took you one good word.

summary: Every dead letter went light. Posy cried on the franking machine.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Delivery for you — sort of. Ellery’s been rereading one empty bookplate all week and pretending she isn’t. Go see her, would you? Some parcels need legs.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Tell her the string’s from me. She’ll know what it means. It doesn’t mean anything — that’s the joke. We’ve had it forty years.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: She’ll deny the fretting, mind. Librarians grieve in reshelving. You’ll see it if you look slant.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And walk slow on the Library stairs. News keeps. Friends keep better.

summary: Posy’s errand: Ellery is fretting over an empty bookplate.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Second item: Fern’s been standing about the Conservatory like an unwatered hat-stand. Something about a bloom. She won’t ask for help. That’s what I’m for.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Don’t say I sent you. Say you were passing. She can smell an errand at forty paces.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Take her something green if you find it. Or say something short. She trades in short.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: She’s softer than the boots suggest. Most standing things are.

summary: Posy’s errand: Fern is waiting on a bloom and won’t ask for help.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Now — a personal favor, strictly off the books. There is a word for the smell of rain on warm dust. The master knew it. I lost it. It’s somewhere in this house.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: He used it in a letter once, and I have spent years failing to re-read it from memory. Shake his rooms hard enough and it will fall out. Words do.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I know the shape of it. Starts soft, ends like thunder cooling. Three syllables, I think. Or four. Memory rounds things.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And no — I can’t just requisition it. Words don’t answer forms. Believe me. Form 11-B, Request for a Word. Filed it twice.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: No rush, mind. I’ve waited years; I can wait weeks. It’s the not-looking I couldn’t do anymore.

summary: Posy’s favor: find the lost word for the smell of rain.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: This came overnight — open franking, his hand, no address needed. One word on the page: PETRICHOR. You shook it loose, whatever you did in those rooms.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Petrichor. The smell of rain on warm dust. I’ve said it eleven times this morning and it has rained indoors twice. Worth every year of waiting.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ve written it on the sorting-room wall, small, where only I look. Officially that’s vandalism. I’ve fined myself a biscuit.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Funny thing — the ledger says the word was never lost. Just in transit. Longest delivery of my career, and worth it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You’re in the story now, you know. When I tell it — and I will tell it — there’s a knock at the door and it’s you.

summary: Found Posy’s word: PETRICHOR. It has already rained indoors twice.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: One drawer in this room I never open. A letter he wrote and never posted. No address — just ‘To—’ and then thirty years of the nerve failing.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: It’s not that I forgot it. A postmistress forgets nothing in her care; that’s the whole oath. It’s that remembering is the only delivering I’m allowed.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Thirty years I’ve sorted round that drawer without once opening it. You can wear a groove in a room just by not-looking at one spot in it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: There. Now two of us know. A secret carried in pairs stops rattling — postal wisdom, that, and free with every delivery.

summary: There is an unposted letter in Posy’s drawer, addressed ‘To—’.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You’ll wonder why I don’t deliver his unposted letter myself. Postmistress’s oath: we carry, we don’t decide. He had to want it sent.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: But learn who ‘To—’ was meant for, and I will walk that letter up those stairs personally. Full uniform. Best wax.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I have my suspicions, mind. A postmistress always does. But suspicion isn’t an address, and this one has to be right the first time.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You’re good at finding what this house misplaced. I’m only saying. No pressure, love. Well — postal pressure. The gentle kind.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Until then it stays in the drawer. Safe as houses. Safer — houses wander.

summary: Learn who ‘To—’ is, and Posy will deliver the letter herself.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Deputy’s sash. Go on, take it — you’re Post Office staff now, which means the house is obliged to tell you things in writing. Use it wisely. Or nosily. Both work.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Duties: nosiness, kindness, and the defense of string. Benefits: first look at the morning sort and my unqualified fondness. You had that last one already.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The sash was mine, when I started. Fifty years of pockets. There’s a peppermint in the left one from an era when peppermints were better.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Wear it Sundays, or never, or always. The house knows what it means either way.

summary: Sworn in as Posy’s deputy. The house must tell you things in writing.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: For me? Oh, that’s going straight in the ledger under ‘valuables, sentimental, uninsurable.’ Best heading I ever invented and I have waited years to use it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Here — my spare letter-opener. Brass. Opens envelopes, jammed drawers, and most kinds of silence.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Careful with the point — it has opened fifty years of other people’s news and it’s kept every bit of the edge.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And mind it around Dewey. He believes all brass is his. He’s not entirely wrong; that’s the trouble.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: When it opens something that changes your day, come tell me. That’s the fee. Payable in gossip, as all the best debts are.

summary: Gave Posy a bookmark; received her brass letter-opener.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The manor has its own postmark, you know. A little house with too many windows. Accurate.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Look close and the windows in the postmark shift, printing to printing. Nobody engraves that. I’ve stopped asking how; the asking spoils the trick.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Collectors would weep for it. Let them. Some things aren’t for albums; they’re for envelopes.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ll stamp you a spare on an envelope corner, if you like. Everyone should own proof their house exists.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Count the windows some morning. Count them again after tea. Don’t come to me about the difference — I stopped counting in ’74 and I sleep beautifully.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Hardest part of the job? Rooms move overnight and forwarding addresses don’t exist. I deliver by intuition and mild threats.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Once delivered the same parcel to the same door three days running. Different room behind it every time. All three signed for it. Bureaucracy finds a way.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: If a corridor looks new, walk it before noon. Rooms are shy their first day, and it’s polite to visit early.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You get a feel for it, in time. The house moves like a sleeper, not a stranger. Roll with it and nothing lands on you.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Dewey sleeps in the parcel bin. Anything he sits on gets priority handling — cat-certified. It’s an excellent system and I did not design it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: He knows which parcels matter, is the thing. Sat a whole week on a box of seeds once and wouldn’t budge till Fern came for it. Cats read futures. Ours just reads freight.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I pay him in the string ends. He is the only staff member who has never once complained about wages.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Official position: the Post Office does not employ a cat. The cat employs us. It’s tidier, legally.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: People underestimate string. Empires of correspondence, held together by string and someone who cares.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The master sent for string from six counties. Said the local stuff had no memory. He was wrong, but he was wrong carefully, and that’s the best kind of eccentric.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: You can tell a parcel wrapped in love from one wrapped in duty by the knots alone. Yours, incidentally, would be love. Bit clumsy. Love usually is.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: There’s a ball of it in my drawer from my first week here. Retired now. We’ve been through things, that string and I.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Six counties, and the local stuff had the best memory of the lot. I never told him. Some corrections are just unkindness with a footnote.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: A bill arrived for the master today. Thirty years late. I stamped it ‘DECEASED — TRY THE PORTRAIT’ and felt wonderful about it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: It came back this morning marked ‘ADDRESSEE OTHERWISE ENGAGED.’ The Portrait has developed a correspondence style. Heaven help the utilities.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ve framed the envelope. Some paperwork is simply art with a due date.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The gas company writes such passionate prose when ignored. Fifty years of it. The longest correspondence this house has ever kept, arguably.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Those fragments you’re collecting — that’s a correspondence, you know. Him to you. When you’re ready to reply, the address is the top of the stairs.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: And when you write back — because that’s what the guess is, love, a reply — sign it like yourself. Doors read signatures the way I read wax.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: One word a day is good postage discipline, anyway. Makes you choose. Choosing is nine-tenths of writing.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Whatever the door says back, come tell me. Good news wants witnesses. Bad news wants tea. Either way you know where I am.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Bramble and I trade: tea for stamps. The exchange rate is friendship, and neither of us audits it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: She claims my stamps for the household accounts, then posts nothing. I claim her tea for the afternoon sort, then sort nothing. It’s a flawless economy.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Four o’clock sharp, mind. The kettle is the one punctual thing in a house that eats clocks.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Sit in on it some afternoon. We’ll say it’s official business. Everything’s official if the tea’s hot.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The afternoon sort waits for no one, dear heart — not even you, and you’re the best part of the day it’s interrupting.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Go on — anything urgent, I’ll send a boy. We haven’t got a boy. I’ll send the cat.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Some of us have a kingdom of brown paper to run, and it does not run itself, whatever the string may claim.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: First thing tomorrow, mind. I’ll save you the good stamp and the better half of the gossip.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Posy deals envelopes into pigeonholes like a card sharp — lips moving, counting rooms that may not exist yet.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Without looking up: a small wave, a smaller smile, and an envelope slid to the counter’s edge with your name on it. There is nothing inside. It’s the principle.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The pile on the left is shrinking. The pile on the right is not growing. Postal arithmetic answers to no one.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Thunk. Thunk. The franking stamp keeps better time than the hall clock, and both of them are lying.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Between thunks, Posy mouths the room names like a psalm: parlor, gallery, kitchen, hush.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Shall I tell you what I do first now? Before the kettle, before the sort — I check your pigeonhole. Fifty years of routine, dear heart, rearranged round one square of brass.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Shocking practice. A postmistress sorts by room, not by fondness. I have no intention whatever of correcting it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Another bookmark for the ledger! ‘Valuables, sentimental, uninsurable’ is becoming my thickest file, and it is entirely your fault.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ve started rotating them so none of them feels like a spare. Yes, they have feelings. Everything in this room has feelings; it’s the humidity.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Off you go, love. You can’t stand about being generous all day — there’s a schedule.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: A room went unfinished yesterday — no, don’t look caught out, the house sends me the manifests. Unfinished isn’t undelivered, love. It’s in transit.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I keep a whole shelf for in-transit. Cozier than it sounds. Everything on it gets where it’s going eventually.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Besides — a room mid-puzzle is a room with something to look forward to. Enviable, really.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The cat came through here purring like a franking machine. Your doing, I hear. He’s told everyone. He has no discretion and we love him anyway.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: One step for a pet is the best exchange rate in the building. Don’t tell the economy.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: He’s filed your kindness under permanent record, mind. Cats keep the only archives that never burn.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Every pigeonhole is a room’s whole biography, if you read it right. The Gallery’s gets postcards. The Kitchen’s gets recipes and apologies.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Yours? Yours gets thicker by the week, love. I’ve had to move the Conservatory up a row. Pollen and all.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Come read yours whenever you like. It’s your biography. You’re allowed.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The house writes at night. I’ve heard the nib through the floor — a scratching in the joists, patient as woodworm but kinder spelling.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I leave ink out for it now. The level drops. That’s between us and the floorboards.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ve thought about staying up to catch it at the writing. Decided against. Some correspondents deserve their privacy.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: It writes better than it spells, mind. Or spells better than it writes. Depends entirely which floor you’re standing on when you read it.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: My first week, I dropped a whole sheet of stamps behind the counter. Found them last spring — the house had filed them by color. Fifty years late and alphabetized. That’s this place all over.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Nothing’s lost here, love. It’s all just very, very patient.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ve stopped dropping things on purpose, mind. The house grades on presentation.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Before letters, this room did telegrams. STOP after every thought. Ghastly way to speak.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: The machine’s under a sheet in the corner. It clacks once a year, on the master’s birthday. We’ve never traced the sender.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I write the message down anyway. Every year. It’s always just: STILL HERE. STOP. Good message, as they go.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I’ve drafted a reply eleven times. STILL HERE TOO. STOP. Never sent one. Wouldn’t know where to send it, and that’s the trouble with a good message.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Posy is winding string from one ball onto another ball. There is, as far as can be told, no difference between the balls. She seems deeply content.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: Your file’s getting properly thick — which means it’s time. One item I never posted into anyone’s pigeonhole, because it was his.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: His last letter went out with one word cut clean from it. A little window in the paper. You could read the whole sentence around the hole.

lines.speaker: posy
lines.text: I believe that was rather the point. First-class evidence, that. Consider it delivered.

summary: Posy’s testimony: the letter with a window cut in it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You’re new. The plants said. They notice feet.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Feet say a lot. Yours say curious. Good start.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Mind the ivy by the door. Friendly. Too friendly.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Boots stay on indoors here. Garden’s everywhere. You’ll see.

summary: Met Fern, the groundskeeper. The plants noticed you first.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Fern. Groundskeeper. Yes, really Fern. My mother thought she was funny. She was.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: She kept grounds before me. Her mother before that. Ferns all the way down.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: One of us was bound to grow up literal.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Call me Fern either way. Everything answers to green here eventually.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Listen low. Growing’s loud, if you’re patient.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Roots gossip. Leaves eavesdrop. A garden’s just a slow conversation.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You’ll learn the language. First word’s always ‘water’.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Second word’s usually ‘more water’. Plants are simple. It’s their best quality.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Garden’s indoors here. Rooms grow like beds — some seasons you get nettles. Bring me seeds if you find any. I trade fair.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Nettles aren’t a punishment, mind. House grows what it’s feeling. Some days that’s roses. Some days it stings.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Seeds turn up in odd corners. Drawers. Hems. One in a teapot once. Bramble still brings it up.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Bring me any you find. Fair trade, always. I don’t haggle. Gardens taught me patience, not commerce.

summary: Fern trades fair, if you bring her seeds.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Every petal, one word. Whole flower at once. Don’t tell the roses — competitive, roses.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Whole alphabet, one flower. Doesn’t happen twice a season.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The bees will talk about it for days. Let them. Winters are long.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Good hands. Said it before. Saying it again. Repetition’s how gardens compliment.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Full Bloom in the Conservatory. Smelled it from the stairwell. Good hands.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Thirty years since the glass sweated like that. Place remembers how to be warm. Just needed reminding.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Bramble asked what smells different. Told her: spring. Indoors. In whatever month this is. She dusted at it suspiciously.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Come stand in it sometime. Bloom’s better shared. Most things are, I’m told.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Every petal. The whole hundred. Once a decade, that. The master managed it twice and bragged for years — quiet-like, but he bragged.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I pressed one petal. For the record. Groundskeeper’s privilege.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He’d have stood here an hour, hat off. So I did it for him. Felt right.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Don’t do it again too soon. Miracles keep best rationed.

summary: Every petal in the Conservatory. Fern was almost effusive.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Conservatory’s humming again. You planted well today.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The comb’s gone gold at the edges. That’s contentment, in bee.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The queen approves. I know because nothing stung me all morning. That’s bee for ‘well done’.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Same tomorrow, if you like. Garden holds no grudges about yesterday. Only lesson it ever taught me twice.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Left the garden mid-bloom? It keeps. Gardens are patient. It’s their whole trick.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The flowers you did find are still standing. Growth keeps. That’s the whole contract.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The bees marked your tab. They’re fair about it. Fairer than banks.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Come back when you come back. That’s the whole rule here.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Cat’s been bragging. Wears your pets like a medal. One step’s cheap for that much smug.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He naps in the seed trays after. Warm dirt, warm cat. System works.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Keep petting him. Cheapest good deed in the building, and he banks every one.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He’ll expect it daily now. You’ve made a contract. Cat law’s strict.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: House shivered last night. Felt it in the roots. Wrong word. Roots held. They always hold.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Wrong guesses are pruning. Looks brutal. Isn’t. You’re shaping the thing.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Roots don’t rush. Neither should you. Door’s not going anywhere. Doors famously don’t.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Every ‘no’ narrows the bed. Fewer weeds each pass. That’s progress wearing its work clothes.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Found one of his papers. He buried words like bulbs. Figured someone would come along with the right spring.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Hold it flat and let it warm. Paper relaxes. Tells you more relaxed.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He’d be glad it’s your hands. Careful ones. Bulbs know the difference.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Keep it dry, keep it flat. Same rule as seeds. Same reason.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: No missteps yesterday. Like watching frost mind its own business. Tidy.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: No wasted moves. Garden calls that grace. So do I, on the days I talk.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Don’t chase it, mind. Chased grace trips. Just walk like that again tomorrow.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The floors mentioned it. Floors notice grace first. All that weight on them.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Walked yourself to stubble yesterday. Even fields lie fallow. There’s a bench in here that does nothing. Use it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Fallow’s not idle. Fields do their best work looking useless. Learned that the slow way.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Bench is under the fig. Does nothing beautifully. Join it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I’ll know if you didn’t. The bench reports to me.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Morning after you said it, every pot in the Conservatory flowered. Out of season. All of them. I sat down on the nothing bench for a while.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He used to say gardens forgive first. Now the rest of the house has caught up.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The rosebush held its bloom a full week after. Out of respect, I’d say. Roses understand occasions.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I told the garden he could rest now. Roots passed it down. Whole house heard by supper, my way.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Come dig with me some morning. No reason. That’s the point of it now.

summary: Every pot flowered out of season. Gardens forgive first.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Planted for him thirty years. He’d name seedlings in Latin. Wrong Latin, mostly. Never corrected him. You don’t prune a man’s joy.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He’d sit on an upturned pot and read me definitions while I weeded. Said the garden improved his spelling. Nonsense. He just liked company that didn’t argue.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: ‘Fern,’ he’d say, ‘this seedling is Quercus ridiculus.’ Wasn’t. Wasn’t even an oak.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I’d give a good spade to hear the wrong Latin again.

summary: Fern never corrected the master’s Latin. You don’t prune joy.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: After the word went, he stopped coming down. Garden waited. I waited. Waiting’s just planting with no seed. Wouldn’t recommend it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I sent shoots up under his window. Green’s a knock, if you do it slow. He never answered.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Grief’s a hard frost. Some things come back after. Some don’t. He didn’t get his after. That’s the whole sadness of him.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You’re the after, I reckon. Late spring. Still spring.

summary: After the erasure, the garden waited. So did Fern.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Posy sent you? Meddler. Fine. The old rosebush won’t open till the Conservatory blooms proper — Full Bloom, the whole garden singing. Bring it up and I’ll owe you.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: It was his rosebush, strictly. I’ve kept it alive. Alive isn’t open. Open takes joy, and joy wants a whole garden behind it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: That’s the horticulture. Rest is up to your hands.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Ask the bees for the corners you can’t reach. They owe me one. Several.

summary: Fern’s favor: bring the Conservatory to Full Bloom for the rosebush.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Rosebush opened this morning. Not bloomed since before he went. White, with a temper of pink at the edges.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: He planted it for someone. Never said who. Now it can say it for him.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I sat with it an hour this morning. Didn’t weed. Didn’t prune. Just sat. First idle hour I’ve spent in years that didn’t itch.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Thirty years is nothing to a rose, turns out. Just long enough to mean it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Come see it before it drops. Some things you owe your own eyes.

summary: The rosebush opened — first time in thirty years.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Here. Key to the seed vault. Every room this house ever grew, sleeping in paper packets. Plant what you like. You’ve earned dirt-rights.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Vault’s behind the potting bench. Key sticks. Lock’s sentimental.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Some packets are labeled in his Latin. Plant those blind. Best surprises in the house.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Dirt-rights aren’t nothing, mind. I’ve given out two sets in my life. Other one’s buried with him.

summary: Earned dirt-rights: the key to Fern’s seed vault.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Oh. For me, is it. I press leaves — have since I was nine. Never once had something pretty handed me to press beside them.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Take the seed tin. Rattle it near a door you want tomorrow. Superstition. Works, though.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Pressed a sweet-pea leaf beside it already. They’ll keep each other flat.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Rattle the tin gentle, mind. Seeds startle. Everything young does.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Tin’s older than me. Passed hand to hand, always dirt-first. Keep the tradition.

summary: Gave Fern a bookmark; received her rattling seed tin.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Moss gets a bad name. Patient stuff. Covers what the house regrets.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: There’s moss on the north wall older than the deeds. Outlasted three roofs. Never once hurried.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I consult it on hard decisions. Sits there. Very wise.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Sit by it when the house feels loud. Nothing hurries near moss. Catching.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Take a cutting if you like. Won’t take. Moss goes where moss decides. Good lesson in that.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: No sky in here, but the Conservatory invents its own weather. Tuesdays it drizzles. We’ve an understanding.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Wednesdays it’s sun, wherever the real sky stands. The glass just decides.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Drizzle days are best for planting. Come Tuesday, if you want dirt under your nails and no talking.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Mind the fig on drizzle days. Drips down collars. Thinks it’s funny.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Sharp spade, soft heart. Only rule of grounds-keeping worth keeping.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: His trowel’s still on the third hook. Oiled. Handle worn to his grip.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Not a shrine. A tool waiting. Different things entirely. One of them’s hope.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Take the second-hook trowel if you fancy digging. Good handle. No history. History’s heavy in a tool.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Cat helps me garden. Supervises. Sits on the trowel at quitting time. Union cat.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Filed a grievance once. Sat on my seed catalogue till I opened the good window. Grievance upheld.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Best foreman I’ve had. Sleeps on the job and the job improves.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Never feed him in the Conservatory, mind. He’ll expect soil rights. Slippery negotiator.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Rooms grow faster upstairs. Richer soil, or richer secrets. Same thing, in a house.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Cellar rooms come up mushroomy. Quick, quiet, gone by Thursday. Attic rooms take all season and keep forever.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Same as people, roughly. Don’t quote me to the attic.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The Study grew slowest of all. Some rooms wait for their person. Still waiting, that one. Warmer lately, though.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: His papers you’re gathering — seeds, those. Don’t go up on a half-grown one. Wait till the whole bed comes ready at once. That’s harvest. Top of the stairs, and go gentle.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Don’t force the harvest, mind. Green fruit teaches nothing but patience, the loud way.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You’ll know ripe. Everyone does. It’s the one wisdom nobody has to be taught.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: And take water up with you. Long stairs. Dry work, truth.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Watering hour. Can’t talk through it. Plants count the gaps.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Plants first. You understand. You’re the sort that understands.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: That’s me emptied. Fills again by morning, like the water butt.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Go stand somewhere green till then. Standing’s growing, technically.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Fern waters a fern. Neither remarks on it. Some jokes are thirty years deep and still bearing.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: She tips the last of the can into a pot that holds, as far as anyone knows, plain dirt. ‘Early days,’ she says, to the dirt.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Snip. A single yellow leaf drops. Fern pockets it like a coin.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The leaf goes in a left pocket that bulges with a season of such coins.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Fern hums two notes, over and over. The vines nearest her keep time.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You almost catch the tune. It’s older than the house. The vines clearly know the words.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: That bed by the east glass. The unnamed one. Stopped saving it Tuesday.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Wrote a name on the marker. Not telling you which. Come back in spring and read it yourself.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Another one? You’ll spoil the pressing book.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: It’s gone in beside the sweet-pea. Growing quite the meadow of ribbon in there.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Go on, now. Kindness that stands about gets planted, and you’ve things to do.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You had post this morning. Posy hummed all through her rounds. She only hums for the good deliveries.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Letters are pressed flowers with more words. Keep them flat and out of the sun.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Read it twice. Second read’s the one that keeps.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The garden’s been leaning your way lately. Whole beds of it. I don’t correct them.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Means you’re rooting here. Took me three winters. You’re quicker.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Roots don’t announce. You’ll notice when something tries to move you and can’t.

summary: The garden leans your way now. Fern does not correct it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Heard the Gallery’s chimes from here. Word after word after word. Like rain deciding to be a river.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The paintings straighten themselves when it goes well. Vain room, the Gallery. Earned it today.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Good work. The kind that echoes.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: First frost, I cover the tender beds with his old dust-sheets. House lends them. Never asks for them back till spring.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The statues underneath look like shy ghosts. Ellery says it’s crowded feeling. She’d know.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Sheets come off in March. Everything under them still there. Every year. Still gets me.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I name the long beds after words he liked. Vestibule bed. Petrichor bed. Grows better, named. Everything does.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: There’s an unnamed bed by the east glass. Been saving it. No rush. Names come when they come.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: House never lets it snow indoors but once a year. One night. One corridor. Nobody knows which till it’s ankle-deep.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I leave a shovel out anyway. Tradition. The shovel’s never once been needed and never once been optional.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Stand in it if you find it. One night a year. Snow indoors is a thing you’re allowed to have.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Compost’s just patience with a smell. Everything the house is done with goes in. Comes back soil.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Best batch I ever turned had his old blotting paper in it. Roses that year spelled things, I’d swear.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Don’t look like that. It’s the politest resurrection going.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: The bees came with the house. No one keeps them. They keep us, near as I can tell.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: They dance their directions, you know. Lately the dances point up the stairs. Bees know where the sweetness is stuck.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Take the hint or don’t. They’ll dance it again tomorrow. Patient as sums.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Came the spring he went quiet. Nobody sent for them. Never worked out who told them there was room.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: House does autumn in one hallway only. Keeps it like a jar of something. Leaves down all year.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Walk it slow if you find it. Crunch is good for thinking.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: I sweep it Sundays. It’s back by Monday. Best arrangement I have with anything.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: My mother kept these grounds when the master was young. Her hands in every bed. Mine over hers now, like tracing.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: She told me: gardens don’t die, they change hands. Took me years to hear the kindness in it.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Your hands are in it now too. Noted in the soil, that. Soil keeps records ink would envy.

summary: Gardens do not die; they change hands. Yours are in it now.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: A tray of seedlings sits in the warm. Fern turns it a quarter, so they all get their fair look at the light.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: You keep finding pieces. Here’s mine.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Bed in the west garden. Nothing grows there. He’d stand at it an hour at a time. Said there was a word for that exact shape of missing.

lines.speaker: fern
lines.text: Said he meant to see it filled again. Plants remember. So do I.

summary: Fern’s testimony: the empty bed in the west garden.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: So. The house has let another one climb this far. State your business with my door — no. Don’t. I know your business. Everyone wants the word.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: I am — I was — the lexicographer of this house. The Portrait will do. He is all of me the frame could hold.

summary: Met the Portrait on the landing. He is all the frame could hold.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Flattery. The paint absorbs it; none reaches me. Still — thank you. It has been quiet up here.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: I un-happened it. That is all the door will get from me, and rather more than you have earned before breakfast.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Understand the terms. The door wants the word spoken — once a day, no more. I do not set the rules. I merely became them.

summary: The Sanctum’s terms: one spoken word per day.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: No. Not a letter of it true. The door didn’t even creak. Go and read more of him — of me — before you spend tomorrow’s breath.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Wrong — and one solitary letter of it true, which is not a foothold. The alphabet manages that much by accident, reader.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Wrong. And yet the hinges shifted. Some of those letters belong to the word. You are circling, reader. Circle tighter.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: The right shape. The wrong soul. You have measured the hole in the dictionary exactly — now find what actually fell through it.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: You have said that word to this door before. It was not the word then. Doors do not change their minds; neither, it appears, do you.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Three wrong words, and still you climb back up. Persistence. She had it too — no. Never mind.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Today’s word missed as the others did, and the door’s verdict on it is struck into your journal beside it. Read your own margins. Guess again tomorrow.

summary: The Portrait almost mentioned someone. ‘She had it too.’

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Do you know what it costs a portrait to hope? The varnish cracks. Six wrong words now, and still I find I want you to manage it. Curious.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: This one missed too, and the journal has kept what it was worth, as the journal keeps everything. Go and read your own margins. I shall be here. I am always here.

summary: The varnish is cracking. The Portrait wants you to succeed.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: ...You said it. Out loud. In my house. Thirty years I kept that door shut on it, and you hand it back like a dropped glove.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: I spent the end of a life unwriting that word, because grief with a pen believes erasure is mercy. It is not. It is only quiet.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Thank you for returning it. To the books. To the door. To me.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: For the first time in thirty years, the Portrait is smiling in his frame.

summary: The word came home. The Portrait smiled.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: You have been gathering my scraps. Yes — I know my own hand when it walks past in a pocket. Read them in order, reader. I wrote them out of it.

summary: The fragments were written out of order. Deliberately.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: You have read more of me now than anyone living. I would object, if it weren’t such a relief to be legible again.

summary: The Portrait finds it a relief to be legible again.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: A bookmark. Tucked into my frame as though I were mid-chapter. I have not been mid-anything in thirty years.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Leave it there. Let the house see that the old man is still being read.

summary: Left a bookmark in the Portrait’s frame. He is still being read.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Mind the last stair. It squeaks in iambs. I had it built that way, so nothing could sneak up on a thought.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Bramble dusts my frame on Thursdays and tells me the news. I pretend not to listen. She pretends I am not pretending. A sound arrangement.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: The cat sits on the landing some nights and stares at me. I stare back. So far it is a draw, though he has the advantage of blinking.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: The door stands easier now. So do I. Odd, how a frame can feel like a window once the word is back in circulation.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: So. You climbed it. Six storeys of other people’s rooms, and the last stair squeaking in iambs, and here you are at my door with your hat still crooked. Very well: it wants no key. It wants the word.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Up again. The house notices, you know — it puts the stairs back in the same order for people it expects. One word a day, reader, whenever you are sure of one.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: You have nothing left in your legs, and you spent it getting to me. Sit a moment on the top stair; the door is in no hurry. Then say your word, and let the evening close on it either way.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Your journal is empty, reader. Nothing filed, nothing struck through. The house keeps me in engravings, in memories, in the post. The door will still hear whatever you bring it.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: A thin file, reader. The rooms above hold more of him — of me — and thin files make for expensive guesses. Speak anyway, if you like. The door is not proud.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: The Portrait regards you. Paint cannot blink; he manages the impression regardless.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: We have spoken today. A portrait must ration himself, or become wallpaper.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: The candle bracket beneath the frame is always lit. No one in the house will admit to lighting it.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Another ribbon, for a man made of varnish. You do know I cannot hold it.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: ...Tuck it in the frame, then. Left corner. The dust there has been wanting a reason.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: You. Before you go — I will say this once, and to no one’s question.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: I did not destroy it. I unhoused it. There is a difference — and the difference is the word.

lines.speaker: portrait
lines.text: Write it down. I shall not repeat myself.

summary: The Portrait, unprompted: he did not destroy it — he unhoused it.
